immigration.headline: Under President Trump’s Leadership, USCIS Takes Unprecedented 2.2 Million Enforcement Actions Protecting Americans Across the Nation
immigration.body: Under the leadership of President Donald J. Trump and Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is delivering on the Administration’s agenda and putting the American people first.

immigration.headline: Suburban Chicago Man Sentenced for Staging Robberies to Help Others Fraudulently Apply for Immigration Visas
immigration.body: A suburban Chicago man has been sentenced to two years in federal prison for conspiring to stage armed robberies so purported victims could apply for U.S. immigration visas reserved for crime victims.

immigration.headline: Aliens in Idaho Charged for Illegal Voting
immigration.body: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services assisted an investigation that resulted in charges against two Canadian aliens residing in eastern Idaho for unlawfully voting in the 2022 general election.

immigration.headline: Grocery Store Manager Convicted of Immigration Document Fraud, Obstruction of Two Federal Labor Investigations, and Conspiracy
immigration.body: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services provided pivotal assistance to the case resulting in the conviction of Karla Montoya, 45, of Sacramento.

immigration.headline: Six Charged in Large-Scale Marriage Fraud Ring
immigration.body: Six individuals in Massachusetts have been charged with allegedly arranging sham marriages to fraudulently obtain immigration status for illegal aliens.

immigration.headline: Canada refocusing Express Entry on top talent that drives economic growth
immigration.body: October 16, 2026—Kitchener, Ontario—Building a stronger Canada means restoring confidence in a well-managed immigration system that meets our economic needs. This includes attracting and retaining skilled talent to complement the Canadian workforce and drive economic growth.

immigration.headline: Canada is supporting new projects to promote Francophone immigration and strengthen Francophone minority communities
immigration.body: Collaboration is essential to addressing Canada’s workforce needs and responding to the realities facing Francophone communities. Given the challenges posed by labour shortages and the ongoing need to attract and retain talent, Canada is joining forces with its partners and reinforcing its commitment to Francophone immigration.

jobs.body: Canada's businesses and workers continue to adapt to evolving global trade pressures, including the impacts of tariffs, while building the foundation for future growth.

jobs.body: The world is changing rapidly, and Canada is choosing to build. Major projects across the country will strengthen our economy, diversify trade and create good jobs across the country. Delivering these projects and supporting continued economic growth will require a skilled workforce ready to meet growing demand.
